Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a mutual action plan (attached) that lays out: evaluation criteria, decision checkpoints, and a proposed hosting path for the MCP pilot and production rollouts. High level recommendation is:

- Pilot: Hosted (US-East) for fastest time-to-value and simplified onboarding
- Production: Dedicated reserved capacity (US-East) once throughput hits commit threshold
- Regulated modules: Optionally deployed to Private (VPC/on-prem) for PHI segments if required by legal/regulatory review

Attachments in this email: MCP_MAP_v4.pdf (MAP draft), Security_Questionnaire_MCP.xlsx (initial answers).

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm whether data residency requires strictly private/on-prem for pilot data?
2) Who on your procurement side should we loop in for committed capacity pricing?
3) Any preferred go-live window for pilot (May vs June)?

Proposed week-by-week timeline is in the MAP; if we agree, we can lock a short pilot SOW and do a dedicated-cost estimate by Thursday.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk the MAP.

Best,

Team —

Looping in recommendations and the cost sketch I mentioned to Dylan on the call. I pulled together a short comparison (attached: hosting_costs_v2.xlsx) that shows three buckets: Hosted, Dedicated (1 yr reserve), Private (VPC + infra uplift). High level notes:

- Hosted: lowest front-loaded effort, we can be live in ~3 weeks for a synthetic-data pilot. Monthly unit cost is higher (OPEX) but no infra ops overhead.
- Dedicated: ~6–8 week lead for reservation + infra prep, predictable unit cost and lower per-token price at scale (we assume 1.5M tokens/day for production sizing). Requires procurement commit.
- Private: highest initial uplift (networking + audits) and longer lead time if on-prem. Recommended if legal requires PHI to never leave customer VPC.

Actionable ask for Dylan: please confirm which modules will process PHI in pilot vs production so we can model a hybrid path (hosted pilot for non-PHI, dedicated for PII/PHI post-procurement, private as a retention/backstop). Once Dylan confirms module split, I will finalize the cost columns and a proposed finance-friendly SOW (estimates only).

Attachment: hosting_costs_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with cost lines and assumptions).

Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final MAP + recommended hosting path and next steps (pilot slot May 24)

Hi Sarah / Jacob / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per Lauren's cost breakdown and your residency note, proposed final path:

1) Pilot (May 24 start): Hosted in US-East, scoped to anonymized/synthetic datasets only (low-risk) — timeline: 3-week pilot run.
2) Production cutover (post-pilot + procurement commit): Dedicated reserved capacity in US-East for core inference workload. We recommend a 1-year commit for unit-cost benefits and predictable SLAs.
3) Regulated modules: Any module that processes PHI will be scoped for Private (customer VPC) and scheduled on a separate rollout track with legal/infosec sign-off. Private remains a firm fallback if legal requires it.

Deliverables attached: final MAP (MAP_final_for_signature.pdf) and an updated security questionnaire. Next steps:
- Procurement: please review attached estimate and confirm whether a 1-yr commit is acceptable.
- Sarah: confirm module list that will remain non-PHI for pilot.
- I will circulate a DocuSign SOW (draft) by EOD tomorrow for procurement review.

Doc links: HubSpot deal (see related links) and the shared MAP folder.

If that looks good, I propose we lock the pilot start (May 24) and schedule a 30-minute kickoff for May 25 to confirm test data and telemetry hooks.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
